title: Immobilization of Live Caenorhabditis elegans Individuals Using an Ultra-thin Polydimethylsiloxane Microfluidic Chip with Water Retention
protocol: Select a suitable strain of C. elegans and Escherichia coli depending on the purpose of the experiment.
Maintain the C. elegans at 20 °C on 6 cm Petri dishes containing 10 mL of nematode growth medium (NGM) spread with overnight-incubated E. coli.
Synchronize the developmental stages of C. elegans from the embryo stage if possible.
Use well-fed adult animals, approximately 3-4 days after hatching with a width of about 50-60 µm for optimal fit in microfluidic channels.
Use buffer solutions for on-chip immobilization depending on the experiment's purpose.
Autoclave S basal buffer solution containing NaCl, cholesterol, potassium phosphate, and water.
Autoclave M9 phosphate buffer solution with NaCl, KH2PO4, Na2HPO4, MgSO4, and water.
Prepare wash buffer solution by mixing 1 M pH 6.0 potassium phosphate, CaCl2, MgSO4, gelatin, and water; then autoclaving.
Use wash buffer for conventional microfluidic chips without wettability to maintain moisture in channels.
Cut transparent, biocompatible cover films to a width of 10-15 mm and length of 30-50 mm: 130-170 µm thick cover glass, 125 µm thick polyester (PET) film, and ~130 µm thick polystyrene (PS) film.
Enclose ≥10 washed adult animals in the worm sheet using each cover film respectively for 3 h.
Place ≥10 washed adult animals on a 3.5 cm plate containing 3 mL fresh NGM, cover with a lid, and leave for 3 h.
Remove the cover film from the worm sheet after 3 h of immobilization.
Add a drop of buffer solution to each animal.
Pick up animals swimming in the droplet using a platina picker.
Transfer animals to a 3.5 cm plate containing 3 mL fresh NGM without food (assay plate).
Collect animals after 3 h of free movement on the NGM plate.
Add a drop of buffer solution to each animal after 3 h.
Pick up animals swimming in the droplet using a platina picker.
Transfer animals to an assay plate using a platina picker.
Count 'body bends' manually under a microscope at least 5 min after transfer to the assay plate.
Carry out locomotion assays five times independently for each cover film.
Calculate the average number of body bends for the 10 animals in each group for each experiment.
Average the values from five independent experiments to evaluate the effects of on-chip immobilization.
Analyze the data statistically using a one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) test at significance levels of 0.01 and 0.05.
Wear disposable, sterile gloves to avoid contaminating the worm sheets.
Place a thin transparent sheet, such as a PS or glass cover film, onto the experimental desk or microscopic stage.
Gently place a worm sheet onto the bottom cover film using flat tweezers.
Pick up an individual adult C. elegans from the culture plate under a stereomicroscope using a platinum picker.
Repeat the process to pick up multiple animals if needed.
Place three droplets (5 µL drops) of buffer solution on the surface of a 6 cm non-treated Petri dish.
Transfer washed animals to a droplet and allow them to remove food by swimming.
Wash animals twice in two separate droplets using a platinum picker.
Rinse the animals in another droplet.
Drop 2-3 µL of buffer solution onto the surface of a worm sheet.
Pick up washed animals from the droplet on the Petri dish and transfer them to the droplet on the worm sheet.
Enclose animals in microfluidic channels using a PS cover film over the worm sheet.
Press gently from one end of the sheet to the other to maintain humidity.
Check for movement of the head under a microscope to confirm that each enclosed animal is alive.
Record the number of the channel where each animal is enclosed.
Note the position of each animal in the channel (left/center/right).
Indicate the direction of the head with an arrow on a dedicated sheet of paper.
Remove the cover film from the worm sheet using flat tweezers immediately after immobilization.
Drop 10-15 μL buffer solution onto the microfluidic channels enclosing the animals.
Observe the animals starting to swim in the droplets under a stereomicroscope.
Pick up the animals swimming in the droplet using a platinum picker.
Place the picked-up animals on an assay plate.
Select a fluorescence microscope and mount a digital camera or digital video camera on the microscope to capture images or videos.
Maintain a fluorescent strain of C. elegans as described in section 1.
Use young adult HBR411C. elegans for observation, expressing GCaMP3 in all body-wall muscle cells.
Ensure C. elegans are ≤3 days old and thinner than the width of microfluidic channels (50 or 60 µm).
Observe fluorescent spots using a fluorescence microscope with a digital camera mounted on it.
Capture images to observe calcium-ion wave propagation during dynamic activities such as muscular contraction and extension in HBR4 worms.
Locate the worm sheet enclosing multiple animals on an aluminum frame custom-made for the microbeam-irradiation facility.
Set the worm sheet on the automatic stage for irradiation.
Raise the irradiation sample immediately under (~2 mm) the beam exit based on the monitor image from a microscope located under the automatic stage.
Locate each animal to target with the microbeam irradiation using custom-made software.
Confirm the channel number near the left and right edges of the channels.
Control the automatic stage in the X and Y directions to position the animals just under the beam exit using a remote-control system.
Watch the projection from the microscope located under the automatic stage to roughly tune the irradiation area.
Move the cursor to the irradiation position of the animal to be targeted.
Exit and close the irradiation room after rough positioning.
Move to the adjacent control room to avoid irradiating the operators.
Set the desired number of ion particles for one irradiation procedure using the console linked to an ion-counter system.
Fine-tune the position of the animals based on the monitor image from the microscope under the automatic stage.
Target the microbeam irradiation by clicking the irradiation button of the software.
Place the used worm sheet on a 6 cm Petri dish.
Drop about 100 μL of sterilized ultrapure water onto the whole sheet.
Paddle the water on the surface of the sheet using gloved fingers to wash off dirt such as dust, bacterial food, and any eggs laid in the channels.
Wipe the moisture off the worm sheet thoroughly using disposable wipes.
Inject about 5 mL of 70% ethanol into the Petri dish containing the worm sheet.
Paddle the surface of the sheet using gloved fingers to wash off the dirt.
Remove the chips from the Petri dish filled with 70% ethanol.
Allow the sheets to dry naturally.
Place the dried worm sheet on a sterile Petri dish and cover it.
Store the worm sheet in a sterile Petri dish filled with 70% ethanol if desired.
